# Mail crypto interop fixtures

These messages are test data for `internal/mailcrypto`. They contain no real
secrets and no private keys. The S/MIME fixtures use a self-signed test
certificate generated in a temporary directory; the OpenPGP fixtures use a
temporary test key generated by `ProtonMail/go-crypto`.

Regenerate with:

```bash
cd backend
go run ./cmd/mailcrypto-fixtures
```

OpenSSL must be on `PATH` for the S/MIME fixtures. The generator writes only
messages and a manifest; private key material never leaves its temporary
directory.

| File | Shape |
| --- | --- |
| `plain.eml` | ordinary `multipart/alternative`, no protection |
| `smime-signed.eml` | OpenSSL `multipart/signed` S/MIME |
| `smime-enveloped.eml` | OpenSSL `application/x-pkcs7-mime` enveloped-data |
| `smime-sign-then-encrypt.eml` | signed S/MIME entity encrypted as enveloped-data |
| `pgp-mime-encrypted.eml` | `multipart/encrypted` PGP/MIME |
| `pgp-mime-signed.eml` | `multipart/signed` PGP/MIME |
| `pgp-inline-encrypted.eml` | legacy armored inline PGP message |
| `pgp-inline-signed.eml` | legacy clear-signed PGP message |
| `pgp-key-block.eml` | a public-key block, correctly not treated as protected mail |
| `malformed-signed.eml` | `multipart/signed` with a missing signature part |

`fixtures.json` records the expected protocol, encrypted/signed flags and MIME
kind used by `fixtures_test.go`.

The S/MIME signed fixture intentionally has a headerless first MIME entity,
which is what OpenSSL emits. The analyser must preserve that shape rather than
inventing headers for it.
